dedupe_keys.name: feasible supply of steel and cement within a carbon budget is likely to fall short of expected global demand

description: Takuma Watari and coauthors publish optimisation models for steel and cement supply under carbon budgets. Zenodo archives version 1.0 under CC BY 4.0 and links a public repository with MIT code metadata. The repository README identifies a published Nature Communications study and datasets used to estimate feasible material supply against expected demand. This model can test material-availability constraints in long-run infrastructure build-out simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this global supply formulation; the separate Japanese concrete-cycle model addresses a different resource and scale. Coverage is global scenarios, not individual mine, mill or construction sites. A limitation is that carbon budgets, technology trajectories and demand expectations are scenario assumptions, not forecasts guaranteed by the code. Country distribution, trade and local bottlenecks may need separate modelling. The archive was not downloaded, the optimisation was not run and no supply gap was independently recalculated.
